X.note: The environment is strong: raking light, peeling plaster and rubble. The soldiers are sparse, stiff, mannequin-like figures with simplified flat-colour coats. Some have bare legs, and one is half-naked. The Union Jack flag is distant and tiny. The foreground has some breathing room and a readable focal figure.

Y.note: The environment is identical to X, so the quality is the same. A dense column of near-identical soldiers fills the lane. They look like game assets or paper-doll cutouts: flat colours, repeated cross-belts, faceless heads and thin legs. The crowd is clumped and overlapping. The two foreground figures have blue-grey coats with white cross-belts that look odd. The crowd does read more as a formation or garrison.

why: The set and lighting are identical, but X's sparser, better-spaced figures look less like a copy-pasted toy crowd than Y's clumped, repeated soldiers, although neither set of figures is convincing.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the repeated soldier models in Y with varied, properly proportioned figures: individual faces, tricorne or round hats, correct breeches, gaiters and shoes, uneven spacing, some posture variation and a contact shadow under each. Add depth haze and atmospheric dust on the crowd, and add civilians and carts to break up the uniform formation.
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack with the post-1801 design (St Patrick's cross) cannot be confirmed at this size; a 1782 flag would have only the St George and St Andrew crosses
Soldiers' uniforms are simplified modern-looking tunics, not 1782 coats with lapels and turnbacks
Bare legs and missing gaiters or breeches
Shako-like or cylindrical hats on several figures instead of tricornes or round hats
Window shutters and doors look too clean or modern for the walls
Flagpole looks like a modern bare pole
